subproblem.title: Deformation of the shells: homotopy identities, integrality, mass and support bounds (Simon 6.5.1, (11)–(16), (20), (22)–(23))
subproblem.statement: Deformation of the shells of a decomposed current (Simon Ch. 6, proof of 5.1, displays (11)–(16), (20), (22)–(23)). Let P, m ∈ ℕ and let push_k(F, X) ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P), homot_k(F, G, X) ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^P) be operations (k ∈ ℕ, F, G : ℝ^P → ℝ^P, X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P), domain univ) satisfying (PF), the property that the conclusion of the frozen type of Submission.cmcdt_lipschitz_pushforward_homotopy asserts, for this P, of the operations push and homot it provides (the body after its ∃ push homot, taken verbatim as a hypothesis): calling X normal with compact support (NC) when spt X is compact, M(X) < ∞ and boundaryMassOn X univ < ∞ (= M(∂X) for k ≥ 1, 0 for k = 0), for all Λ ∈ ℝ≥0, all Λ-Lipschitz F, G, F', G' and all NC X, Y of degree k: (1) push_k(id, X) = X; (2) push_k(F, X − Y) = push_k(F, X) − push_k(F, Y) and homot_k(F, G, X − Y) = homot_k(F, G, X) − homot_k(F, G, Y); (3) if F = F' and G = G' on spt X then push_k(F, X) = push_k(F', X) and homot_k(F, G, X) = homot_k(F', G', X); (4) M(push_k(F, X)) ≤ Λ^k M(X), spt push_k(F, X) ⊆ F(spt X), M(homot_k(F, G, X)) ≤ δ(2Λ)^k M(X) whenever δ ∈ ℝ and |F(x) − G(x)| ≤ δ for x ∈ spt X, and spt homot_k(F, G, X) ⊆ {F(x) + t(G(x) − F(x)) : x ∈ spt X, t ∈ [0, 1]}; (5) for X ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^P) with compact support, M(X) < ∞, M(∂X) < ∞: ∂ push_{k+1}(F, X) = push_k(F, ∂X), push_{k+1}(G, X) − push_{k+1}(F, X) − homot_k(F, G, ∂X) = ∂ homot_{k+1}(F, G, X), and if X is integer multiplicity then push_{k+1}(F, X) and homot_{k+1}(F, G, X) are integer multiplicity; (6) for X ∈ 𝒟_0(ℝ^P) with compact support and finite mass, push_0(G, X) − push_0(F, X) = ∂ homot_0(F, G, X). Assume moreover (S-ii) every X ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) (domain univ) has closed support, and (S-iii) spt(A − B) ⊆ spt A ∪ spt B for all A, B ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) (these are conjuncts (ii) and (iii), in degree m, of the frozen type of Submission.cmcsd_support_calculus, taken as hypotheses). Let W_j ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P), D_j, Z_j ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P), φ_j : ℝ^P → ℝ^P, Λ_j ∈ ℝ≥0 (j ∈ ℕ), δ ∈ ℝ and L, A, A' ⊆ ℝ^P, and assume: ∂W_0 = D_0 − Z_0 and ∂W_{j+1} = D_{j+1} − (Z_{j+1} − Z_j) for all j; every W_j is integer multiplicity; spt W_j, spt D_j, spt Z_j are compact, M(W_j), M(∂W_j), M(D_j), M(Z_j) < ∞ and boundaryMassOn D_j ℝ^P, boundaryMassOn Z_j ℝ^P < ∞; φ_j is Λ_j-Lipschitz, 1 ≤ Λ_j and Λ_j ≤ Λ_{j+1}; φ_{j+1} = φ_j on spt Z_j; dist(φ_j(x), x) ≤ δ for x ∈ spt W_j ∪ spt D_j ∪ spt Z_j; φ_j(x) ∈ L for x ∈ spt W_j; spt W_j ⊆ A and spt D_j ⊆ A'. Write id := (x ↦ x) and V_j := push_{m+1}(φ_j, W_j), H_j := homot_{m+1}(φ_j, id, W_j) ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(ℝ^P), Y_j := push_m(φ_j, D_j), E′_j := homot_m(φ_j, id, D_j), L′_j := push_m(φ_j, Z_j), K_j := homot_m(φ_j, id, Z_j). Then: (c1) W_0 − V_0 − (E′_0 − K_0) = ∂H_0; (c2) W_{j+1} − V_{j+1} − (E′_{j+1} − (K_{j+1} − K_j)) = ∂H_{j+1} for all j; (c3) ∂V_0 = Y_0 − L′_0; (c4) ∂V_{j+1} = Y_{j+1} − (L′_{j+1} − L′_j) for all j; (c5) V_j and H_j are integer multiplicity for all j; (c6) for all j, M(V_j) ≤ (2Λ_j)^{m+1}M(W_j), M(H_j) ≤ δ·((2Λ_j)^{m+1}M(W_j)), M(Y_j) ≤ (2Λ_j)^m M(D_j), M(E′_j) ≤ δ·((2Λ_j)^m M(D_j)), M(L′_j) ≤ (2Λ_j)^m M(Z_j) and M(K_j) ≤ δ·((2Λ_j)^m M(Z_j)) (in [0, ∞], δ read as ENNReal.ofReal δ); (c7) for all j, spt V_j ⊆ L ∩ cthickening(δ, A), spt H_j ⊆ cthickening(δ, A), spt Y_j ⊆ cthickening(δ, A') and spt E′_j ⊆ cthickening(δ, A') (Metric.cthickening). Conventions: ℝ^P = Euclid P (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P)); for U ⊆ ℝ^P, 𝒟^k(U) = TestFormOn U k (smooth k-forms on ℝ^P whose compact tsupport lies in U) and 𝒟_k(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U k (SimonGMT Chapter06), X(ω) the value of X on ω; X − Y is the contract subtraction, (X − Y)(ω) = X(ω) − Y(ω) (definitional); ∂X = X.boundary, ∂X(η) = X(dη) (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply, dη = exteriorDerivativeTestOn U k η, whose underlying form is exteriorDerivative η); currents are equal when their values agree (GeometricCurrentOn.ext). |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α is the Euclidean coefficient norm of a covector. M_G(X) = X.massOn G ∈ [0, ∞] is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal X(ω) over the ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x (such ω are admissible for M_G, massAdmissibleOn U k G); M(X) = X.mass = M_U(X); boundaryMassOn X G = M_G(∂X) if k ≥ 1 and 0 if k = 0. spt X = X.support (Simon 6.2.11) = U minus the zero region, the union of the open W with compact closure contained in U on which X vanishes (X(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ W). IM = IsIntegerMultiplicity: X is represented by an IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) of the contract, i.e. X(ω) = R.action ω = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ. Metric.cthickening δ E = {x : infEdist x E ≤ ENNReal.ofReal δ}; in a mass bound, a real factor δ is read as ENNReal.ofReal δ.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 0–5 of the parent's supplied proof (Simon Ch. 6, proof of 5.1: the deformed pieces and their mass bounds (11)–(16), the homotopy formula (20) applied to each shell, and the support statements (22)–(23); chapter-06.txt lines 1740–1830), with the homotopy taken from φ_j to the identity (F := φ_j, G := id in (PF)), so that the homotopy currents enter with the signs of (c1)–(c2). Sibling used: MS = cmc_fc_cs_massOn_sub_le (key mass_sub): M_G(A − B) ≤ M_G(A) + M_G(B) for all currents A, B on a common domain and every set G.
Notation. All currents are on univ = ℝ^P and M(X) = M_{ℝ^P}(X). PF1, …, PF5 are the first five conjuncts of (PF) (PF6 is not used). NC_k is the class of X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) with compact support, finite mass and boundaryMassOn X ℝ^P < ∞; PF1–PF4 require their arguments to be NC_k, and PF2–PF5 require all maps involved to be Λ-Lipschitz for one common Λ.
1. (Lipschitz constants.) id is 1-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.id), hence Λ_j-Lipschitz for every j because 1 ≤ Λ_j (LipschitzWith.weaken). φ_j is Λ_j-Lipschitz and Λ_j ≤ Λ_{j+1}, hence also Λ_{j+1}-Lipschitz.
2. (Normality of the pieces.) W_j ∈ NC_{m+1}: spt W_j is compact, M(W_j) < ∞, and in degree m + 1 boundaryMassOn W_j ℝ^P is M_{ℝ^P}(∂W_j) = M(∂W_j) < ∞ by definition. D_j, Z_j ∈ NC_m by hypothesis.
3. (Normality of Z_{j+1} − Z_j.) (a) By (S-iii), spt(Z_{j+1} − Z_j) ⊆ spt Z_{j+1} ∪ spt Z_j, which is compact; by (S-ii), spt(Z_{j+1} − Z_j) is closed; a closed subset of a compact set is compact (IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset). (b) M(Z_{j+1} − Z_j) ≤ M(Z_{j+1}) + M(Z_j) < ∞ by MS (with U = G = ℝ^P). (c) For every n ∈ ℕ and X, Y ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with boundaryMassOn X ℝ^P < ∞ and boundaryMassOn Y ℝ^P < ∞, also boundaryMassOn (X − Y) ℝ^P < ∞: if n = 0 the value is 0 < ∞ by definition; if n = k + 1, then ∂(X − Y) = ∂X − ∂Y, because both currents take the value X(dη) − Y(dη) at every η ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) (definitions of − and ∂; GeometricCurrentOn.ext), so M(∂(X − Y)) ≤ M(∂X) + M(∂Y) < ∞ by MS. Applying (c) with n = m, X = Z_{j+1}, Y = Z_j shows Z_{j+1} − Z_j ∈ NC_m.
4. (Locality.) PF3 with k := m, Λ := Λ_{j+1}, F := φ_{j+1}, G := id, F' := φ_j, G' := id (all four Λ_{j+1}-Lipschitz by step 1), X := Z_j ∈ NC_m, the hypothesis φ_{j+1} = φ_j on spt Z_j and id = id on spt Z_j gives push_m(φ_{j+1}, Z_j) = push_m(φ_j, Z_j) = L′_j and homot_m(φ_{j+1}, id, Z_j) = homot_m(φ_j, id, Z_j) = K_j.
5. (Deforming the boundaries.) (a) PF2 with k := m, Λ := Λ_0, F := φ_0, G := id, X := D_0, Y := Z_0 (both NC_m) gives push_m(φ_0, D_0 − Z_0) = Y_0 − L′_0 and homot_m(φ_0, id, D_0 − Z_0) = E′_0 − K_0. (b) Fix j. PF2 with Λ := Λ_{j+1}, F := φ_{j+1}, G := id, X := D_{j+1}, Y := Z_{j+1} − Z_j (NC_m by step 3) gives push_m(φ_{j+1}, D_{j+1} − (Z_{j+1} − Z_j)) = Y_{j+1} − push_m(φ_{j+1}, Z_{j+1} − Z_j) and homot_m(φ_{j+1}, id, D_{j+1} − (Z_{j+1} − Z_j)) = E′_{j+1} − homot_m(φ_{j+1}, id, Z_{j+1} − Z_j). PF2 again with X := Z_{j+1}, Y := Z_j gives push_m(φ_{j+1}, Z_{j+1} − Z_j) = L′_{j+1} − push_m(φ_{j+1}, Z_j) and homot_m(φ_{j+1}, id, Z_{j+1} − Z_j) = K_{j+1} − homot_m(φ_{j+1}, id, Z_j), and by step 4 the last terms are L′_j and K_j. Hence push_m(φ_{j+1}, D_{j+1} − (Z_{j+1} − Z_j)) = Y_{j+1} − (L′_{j+1} − L′_j) and homot_m(φ_{j+1}, id, D_{j+1} − (Z_{j+1} − Z_j)) = E′_{j+1} − (K_{j+1} − K_j).
6. (Homotopy formula; (c1)–(c5).) PF5 with k := m, Λ := Λ_j, F := φ_j, G := id and X := W_j (compact support, M(W_j) < ∞, M(∂W_j) < ∞) gives: (i) ∂V_j = push_m(φ_j, ∂W_j); (ii) push_{m+1}(id, W_j) − V_j − homot_m(φ_j, id, ∂W_j) = ∂H_j; (iii) since W_j is integer multiplicity, V_j and H_j are integer multiplicity, which is (c5). By PF1 (W_j ∈ NC_{m+1}, step 2), push_{m+1}(id, W_j) = W_j, so (ii) reads W_j − V_j − homot_m(φ_j, id, ∂W_j) = ∂H_j. For j = 0, substitute ∂W_0 = D_0 − Z_0 and step 5(a): (ii) becomes (c1) and (i) becomes (c3). For j + 1, substitute ∂W_{j+1} = D_{j+1} − (Z_{j+1} − Z_j) and step 5(b): (ii) becomes (c2) and (i) becomes (c4).
7. (Mass bounds; (c6).) PF4 with Λ := Λ_j, F := φ_j, G := id, applied to X := W_j (k = m + 1), X := D_j and X := Z_j (k = m), all NC by step 2, gives M(push_k(φ_j, X)) ≤ Λ_j^k·M(X); and, since dist(φ_j(x), id(x)) = dist(φ_j(x), x) ≤ δ for every x ∈ spt X ⊆ spt W_j ∪ spt D_j ∪ spt Z_j, it gives M(homot_k(φ_j, id, X)) ≤ δ·(2Λ_j)^k·M(X).
